projectBrief.whatAreWeBuilding: An institutional-grade In-Memory Electronic Stock Exchange & Limit Order Matching Engine synthesizing TreeMaps, ArrayDeques, HashMaps, and custom Comparators to deliver continuous Price-Time Priority matching and atomic portfolio settlement.
projectBrief.problemItSolves: Financial exchanges (like NASDAQ and NYSE) process millions of limit orders per second. ArrayDeque FIFO queues for Price-Time Priority level buffers

Order book matching algorithm with full and partial fill mechanics

realWorldScenario.headline: Institutional High-Frequency Equities Matching Engine
realWorldScenario.story: You are a quantitative software engineer at a proprietary trading firm building a new low-latency alternative trading system (ATS). Market participants place limit orders to buy (Bids) and sell (Asks) tech equities like AAPL and GOOGL. Your engine must maintain the live order book, execute crossing orders at the resting price, handle partial fills, deduct settlement cash, and stream trade receipts to the consolidated tape.
realWorldScenario.context: Financial markets demand zero mathematical error: bids trade at the highest available price, asks trade at the lowest available price, and trades must balance cash and shares atomically across buyers and sellers.

functional: Define Order entity with orderId, traderId, symbol, side (BUY / SELL), priceCents, initialQuantity, remainingQuantity, and timestamp.
Implement LimitOrderBook for a symbol: Bids in TreeMap<Long, ArrayDeque<Order>> (descending), Asks in TreeMap<Long, ArrayDeque<Order>> (ascending).
Implement continuous Price-Time Priority matching: when Bid price >= best Ask price (or Ask price <= best Bid price), execute matches at the resting order's price.
Support partial fills: decrement remaining quantities; completely filled orders are removed from queue, while partially filled orders retain queue priority.
Implement TraderPortfolio tracking cashCents and Map<String, Integer> share holdings; update buyer and seller portfolios atomically upon trade execution.
Maintain an immutable List<Trade> audit log recording tradeId, buyerId, sellerId, symbol, priceCents, quantity, and timestamp.
Provide an interactive terminal exchange dashboard displaying Market Depth (L2 Order Book), recent trades ticker, and portfolio statements.

Best bid and best ask lookups must execute in O(1) or O(log P) time where P is unique price levels.
Level FIFO insertions and removals must execute in O(1) time via ArrayDeque.
Must compile cleanly with zero warnings under OpenJDK 21 LTS.
userDecisions: Choose between executing trades at the resting order price (standard exchange convention) vs incoming order price.
Select whether to support Market orders (crossing any available price) in addition to Limit orders.

inputsRequired: Order parameters: orderId, traderId, symbol, side (BUY/SELL), price in cents, quantity.

outputsRequired: Level 2 Market Depth display (top 5 bids and top 5 asks).
Trade execution receipt and updated portfolio balance sheets.
variablesNeeded: private final TreeMap<Long, ArrayDeque<Order>> bids: Price descending map.
private final TreeMap<Long, ArrayDeque<Order>> asks: Price ascending map.
private final Map<String, TraderPortfolio> portfolios: Trader cash and equity balances.
private final List<Trade> tradeHistory: Historical ledger.
conditionalLogic: For BUY order: while remainingQty > 0 and !asks.isEmpty() and bestAskPrice <= buyPrice: match orders.
For SELL order: while remainingQty > 0 and !bids.isEmpty() and bestBidPrice >= sellPrice: match orders.
If remainingQty == 0, remove resting order from ArrayDeque; if ArrayDeque is empty, remove price level from TreeMap.
loopStructures: While loop matching orders across book until spread opens or quantity is exhausted.
For-each loop rendering Level 2 market depth table in terminal.
recommendedMethods: public void settleTrade(Order buy, Order sell, long matchPrice, int matchQty)

thinkBeforeYouCode.question: Why do Bids use Collections.reverseOrder() while Asks use natural ordering in TreeMap?
thinkBeforeYouCode.mentorInsight: In financial markets, buyers want to buy as low as possible, but the best buyer is the one offering the HIGHEST price (highest bid first -> reverse order). Sellers want to sell as high as possible, but the best seller is the one offering the LOWEST price (lowest ask first -> natural order).

thinkBeforeYouCode.question: Why must empty ArrayDeques be removed from the TreeMap when all orders at a price level are filled?
thinkBeforeYouCode.mentorInsight: If an empty ArrayDeque remains in the TreeMap, calls to firstKey() or firstEntry() will return a phantom price level with zero available orders, causing NullPointerExceptions or infinite matching loops. Always call map.remove(price) when queue.isEmpty().

thinkBeforeYouCode.question: What is the resting price execution rule in electronic exchanges?
thinkBeforeYouCode.mentorInsight: When an incoming order crosses the spread, the trade executes at the price of the order ALREADY SITTING in the book (the resting order). This rewards liquidity providers who posted quotes first.

hintSystem.level2Implementation: Declare TreeMap<Long, ArrayDeque<Order>> for both sides.

hintSystem.hint: Match min(incomingRemaining, restingRemaining) and update both.
hintSystem.level1Conceptual: Trade quantity is the minimum of what buyer needs and what seller offers.
hintSystem.level2Implementation: Deduct trade quantity from both orders. If resting order is zero, poll it from queue.

normalCases: Place Bid $150 x 10, Place Ask $150 x 10; verify immediate match of 10 shares at $150.00.
Place Bid $150 x 20, Place Ask $150 x 10; verify partial fill of 10 shares, 10 shares remaining on Bid side.
boundaryCases: Incoming Bid price strictly below lowest Ask; verify order rests in book without matching.
Incoming order matches across multiple distinct price levels in a single sweep.
invalidInputCases: Place order with price <= 0 or quantity <= 0; throws IllegalArgumentException.
Trader with insufficient cash attempts to place buy order; rejected with InsufficientFundsException.
edgeCases: Two identical orders placed at same price; verify first arriving order is filled first (FIFO time priority).
All orders at a price level filled; verify price key is completely removed from TreeMap.

debuggingGuide: Infinite matching loop: Check that empty queues are removed from the TreeMap when their size hits 0 (e.g. if (queue.isEmpty()) asks.remove(price);).
Incorrect trade price: Ensure trade executes at the resting order's price, not the incoming order's price.
Spread inverted (Bid > Ask without trade): Ensure match loop executes BEFORE placing the residual quantity into the resting book.

Implement a simulated automated Market Maker generating continuous 2-sided liquidity quotes.

An institutional-grade In-Memory Electronic Stock Exchange & Limit Order Matching Engine in Java synthesizing `TreeMap`, `ArrayDeque`, `HashMap`, and `Comparator` algorithms for continuous Price-Time Priority trading.

## Features
- Continuous Limit Order Book matching engine supporting full and partial fills
- Dual-direction sorted order books (`TreeMap` reverse-ordered for Bids, natural-ordered for Asks)

- Integer-cent financial architecture eliminating rounding drift

## How to Run
```bash
javac StockExchangeDemo.java
java StockExchangeDemo
```

activities.title: Practical Context: The Trading Pit & Two-Sided Auction House
activities.description: How continuous double auctions match buyers and sellers at high speed.
activities.content:
Imagine an auction floor where both buyers and sellers shout quotes simultaneously. On the left side of the room, auctioneers arrange buyers in order of how much they are willing to pay (Bids), with the most generous buyer standing right at the front (highest price first).

On the right side of the room, sellers are arranged in order of the minimum price they will accept (Asks), with the most competitive seller standing right at the front (lowest price first).

When a new buyer shouts a price that meets or exceeds the front seller's price, the auctioneer immediately strikes the gavel, matches the trade at the seller's stated price, hands over the shares, and transfers the cash. If several buyers offer the exact same price, whoever arrived at the microphone first gets filled first (Price-Time Priority).

In Java, `TreeMap` manages the sorted price levels, `ArrayDeque` queues orders at the microphone, and `HashMap` tracks the bank accounts.

activities.title: Architecture of a Limit Order Book & Matching Engine
activities.description: Technical analysis of dual TreeMap sorting, ArrayDeque FIFO priority, and atomic settlement.
activities.content:
### Formal Computer Science Definition
A continuous limit order book is a double auction system represented as two monotonic sorted associative maps: Bids ordered descending $P_{bid} \downarrow$ and Asks ordered ascending $P_{ask} \uparrow$. Each price level contains a FIFO queue $Q_p$ enforcing strict price-time priority. The engine executes matches whenever $\max(P_{bid}) \ge \min(P_{ask})$.

### Limit Order Book Memory Architecture

```
                                ElectronicExchange
                                        |
            +---------------------------+---------------------------+
            |                                                       |
   BIDS (Buy Orders)                                       ASKS (Sell Orders)
   - TreeMap<Long, ArrayDeque<Order>>                      - TreeMap<Long, ArrayDeque<Order>>
   - Comparator: Collections.reverseOrder()                - Natural Order (Ascending)
   - Highest price at firstEntry()                         - Lowest price at firstEntry()
            |                                                       |
            +---------------------------+---------------------------+
                                        |
               [Matching Condition: Best Bid Price >= Best Ask Price]
               - Match executed at RESTING order price
               - Filled quantity = min(bidRemaining, askRemaining)
               - If queue empty -> remove price key from TreeMap
                                        |
               [Atomic Settlement: Ledger Update across Portfolios]
```

### Critical Invariants
1. **Spread Invariant**: When no crossing order is active, $\text{Best Bid} < \text{Best Ask}$. The difference is the bid-ask spread.
2. **FIFO Queue Invariant**: Within each price node, orders must be processed strictly in the order they arrived (`ArrayDeque.pollFirst()`).
3. **Resting Price Rule**: The matched trade executes at the price of the order that was already in the book.

questions.question: Why are Bids stored in a TreeMap with Collections.reverseOrder() while Asks use natural ordering?
options: To prevent deadlocks between buyer and seller threads
Because the best bid is the highest price (firstKey() gets highest), whereas the best ask is the lowest price (firstKey() gets lowest)
Because Bids require 64-bit keys while Asks require 32-bit keys
questions.explanation: Matching engines require instant O(1) access to the best available quote on each side: the highest bid and the lowest ask. Configuring reverse order on Bids places the highest bid at firstKey().

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of using ArrayDeque over LinkedList to store orders at each price level?
options: ArrayDeque is backed by a circular contiguous array, eliminating node pointer overhead and maximizing CPU cache locality
ArrayDeque allows thread-safe writes without locking
ArrayDeque automatically sorts orders by volume
questions.explanation: LinkedList creates a 24-byte Node object for every order, causing garbage collection pauses and CPU cache misses. ArrayDeque uses a contiguous circular array, delivering cache-friendly O(1) FIFO operations.

questions.question: When an incoming market or aggressive limit order crosses the book, at what price does the trade execute under standard exchange rules?
options: At the incoming order's limit price
At the midpoint between the bid and ask
At the price of the resting order that was already in the book
At the previous day's closing price
questions.explanation: In continuous double auction markets, crossing trades execute at the price of the resting order. This incentivizes market participants to supply liquidity by placing resting limit orders.

activities.title: Principal Architect Low-Latency Financial Engineering Interview Questions
activities.description: Staff-level quantitative systems interview queries on matching engine performance and zero-allocation design.

questions.question: How do ultra-low-latency financial matching engines optimize limit order books beyond standard Java TreeMaps?
questions.answer:
In production high-frequency trading (HFT):
1. TreeMaps incur pointer chasing and object allocation on every price insert. Production engines use flat, pre-allocated price-level circular arrays or fixed binary radix trees.
2. Order objects are pooled (zero garbage collection allocations).
3. Fixed-point arithmetic is performed using primitive long primitives directly in CPU registers without boxed Long keys.
4. Core matching logic runs pinned to a single isolated CPU core, using lock-free single-writer ring buffers (Disruptor pattern) to achieve sub-microsecond tick-to-trade latencies.

questions.question: Explain how you guarantee zero monetary leakage when settling millions of concurrent partial fills.
questions.answer:
Financial ledgers enforce double-entry bookkeeping:
1. Every trade execution must produce two equal and opposite entries: (buyer cash - X, seller cash + X) and (seller stock - Y, buyer stock + Y).
2. All math is performed in indivisible integer cents or fractional satoshis/micro-shares (never float or double).
3. Invariant check: The sum of all trader cash plus exchange vault balance must remain invariant before and after trade execution. In unit tests, assert sum(cash_after) == sum(cash_before).
